articles.title: Why Drawing a Black Box Over a PDF Leaks Your SSN (and How I Built a 100% Local Rasterizing Redactor)
articles.excerpt: Every tax season, millions of people try to hide their Social Security Number or account balance on a PDF by drawing a black rectangle in Preview or an online PDF editor. The problem? A black rectangl…
articles.body: Every tax season, millions of people try to hide their Social Security Number or account balance on a PDF by drawing a black rectangle in Preview or an online PDF editor. The problem? A black rectangle is just an annotation sitting on top of the text layer. Anyone who receives that PDF can press Ctrl+A , copy, and paste the "redacted" SSN straight into Notepad. Even worse, most web-based redaction tools require you to upload your unredacted W-2, paystub, or legal contract to their servers first. How True Client-Side Redaction Works When building SafePDFRedact , I wanted two guarantees: Zero network uploads (the tool keeps working even if you turn off Wi-Fi). Irreversible redaction (zero recoverable text layer and zero leftover PDF metadata).
articles.author: YuMir

articles.body: Um glossário técnico precisa de contexto para ser útil. Ao estudar materiais da Duraqex, eu manteria cada entrada ligada ao trecho de origem e à forma escolhida para explicá-la em português. Campos que eu usaria Termo original, tradução adotada, definição curta, referência e observação sobre o contexto. Se a mesma expressão assumir sentidos diferentes, criaria entradas distintas com suas respectivas seções. Revisão dos verbos Também registraria se a fonte descreve uma proposta, uma capacidade declarada ou um resultado de teste. Essa distinção deve sobreviver à tradução. Caso contrário, uma nota pode parecer mais conclusiva do que o material que a sustenta. Um teste simples Outra pessoa deve conseguir voltar ao trecho e reconhecer a relação entre ele e a explicação.

articles.body: RagLeap Physical v0.0.6 is released. Physical AI systems need more than capable models. When AI agents interact with robots, industrial processes or simulated physical environments, their actions must be governed by explicit authorization, enforceable safety boundaries and reliable stop mechanisms. That is the engineering direction behind RagLeap Physical , an open-source project within the RagLeap ecosystem. Version 0.0.6 focuses on strengthening these foundations through safety fixes, observation-only data adapters, adversarial testing and improved runtime behaviour. The project remains pre-alpha and simulation-only . It does not control real machines or production hardware. GitHub: https://github.com/ragleap/ragleap-core/tree/main/packages/ragleap-physical 1.

articles.title: The Light Turns On By Itself: A Field Guide to Automation Conflicts
articles.excerpt: It is 10:30 at night. You switch off the living room light, lie down, and two minutes later it is on again. Over the past six months, posts about lights turning on in the middle of the night — and sma…
articles.body: It is 10:30 at night. You switch off the living room light, lie down, and two minutes later it is on again. Over the past six months, posts about lights turning on in the middle of the night — and smart toilets flushing on their own — have been showing up all over home-renovation forums. Half the replies say "mine does that too," and the other half tell everyone to go check the wiring. I have worked with lighting for more than a decade, and I'll start with the conclusion: in the vast majority of these cases the lamp is not broken. A configuration is running, and usually more than one rule is running at the same time. The light is only the executor. The decisions are being made by a handful of invisible automations you probably forgot you created.

articles.title: SQL Server DATETIME vs DATETIME2: Which to Use, and What Converting an Existing Column Costs
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I build Schemity, a desktop ERD tool - this post is from our blog and uses it for the examples. TL;DR: Use DATETIME2(3) for new columns: it keeps exact milliseconds in 7 bytes, while DATET…
articles.body: Disclosure: I build Schemity , a desktop ERD tool - this post is from our blog and uses it for the examples. TL;DR: Use DATETIME2(3) for new columns: it keeps exact milliseconds in 7 bytes, while DATETIME rounds to steps of 1/300 second in 8. Converting an existing column means dropping its default and indexes first, then a rewrite of every row under a schema lock, about 1.4 seconds and 106 MB of log on one million rows in our test. Pick a precision of 3 or more, or the conversion rounds stored values without an error. For a new SQL Server column, use DATETIME2(3) : it keeps exact milliseconds in 7 bytes, where DATETIME rounds every value to a step of 1/300 second and takes 8. The harder question is the column you already have.

articles.title: Trading Bots vs Humans: Who Actually Wins? A Fair Test
articles.excerpt: Trading bots vs humans: who actually wins? Neither one wins by default. The winner is whichever approach has written rules, honest cost accounting and a large enough sample, and most "bot vs human" co…
articles.body: Trading bots vs humans: who actually wins? Neither one wins by default. The winner is whichever approach has written rules, honest cost accounting and a large enough sample, and most "bot vs human" comparisons online fail on at least one of those three. This guide shows how to run a fair comparison yourself, what bots do better, what humans do better, and where both fail. Trading bots vs humans: who actually wins on what? The question is too broad. It helps to split it into separate jobs. Where bots tend to have an edge Consistency. A bot applies the same rule on trade 1 and trade 400. It does not get bored, angry or overconfident after a streak. Coverage. A bot can watch many pairs around the clock. A person sleeps. Speed of execution.

articles.body: One of Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s strangest random encounters occurs when you’re offering taxi services, and a man with a beard wearing a dark suit and sunglasses climbs into the backseat with a gun. This can happen if you’re playing as either Jason or Lucia, but both scenes play out the same way: The man wants you to run a red light, ignore phone calls, and drive him to Harborside Park in Vice Beach. articles.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
articles.excerpt: How realistic are the zero-g sports we see in sci-fi? We talk to Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, to find out.
articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing after launching into suborbital space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit.

articles.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
articles.excerpt: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station t…
articles.body: Encapsulate Inc. This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments. Orbiting more than 200 miles (320 km) above Earth, the space station is a powerhouse of cutting-edge science that is unlocking discoveries not possible on Earth. Image credit: Encapsulate Inc.
